results.query: Who leads the Aster Program?
results.answer: Helios Research Institute leads the Aster Program with Meridian Labs.

citations.snippet:
Helios Research Institute leads the Aster Program with Meridian Labs. The Aster Program studies the Nereid Basin using the Atlas Sensor. Meridian Labs supplies the Atlas Sensor to Helios Research Institute. The program operates from Zephyr Station.

In 2022, Helios Research Institute approved the Aster Program. In 2024, the Aster Program expanded its Nereid Basin observations.

The 2024 licensing record states that Meridian Labs licensed the Atlas Sensor design to Helios Research Institute for the Aster Program. The license covered three field units and calibration support. Nova Dynamics was not listed as a licensee in this record.

Meridian Labs developed the Atlas Sensor for the Aster Program. The Atlas Sensor sends measurements to Zephyr Station. Zephyr Station forwards processed observations to Helios Research Institute. Meridian Labs maintains the sensor calibration archive.

In March 2024, Meridian Labs delivered the third Atlas Sensor to Zephyr Station. The delivery replaced the prototype sensor used in 2023.

Celeste Analytics analyzed the observations from Zephyr Station and the Atlas Sensor. Celeste Analytics concluded that the Lumen Shelf is the most methane-rich area in the Nereid Basin. Helios Research Institute used the conclusion to prioritize another Aster Program survey.

The causal chain recorded in the report is: Atlas Sensor measurements enabled Zephyr Station processing; Zephyr Station pro

Zephyr Station monitors the Nereid Basin. The Nereid Basin contains the Lumen Shelf, where methane readings are highest. Atlas Sensor observations from Zephyr Station helped Helios Research Institute map the Lumen Shelf.

After the 2024 expansion, Zephyr Station recorded methane and water-vapor signatures at the Lumen Shelf. The findings were reviewed by Meridian Labs.

results.query: When was the Aster Program approved?
results.answer:
Helios Research Institute leads the Aster Program with Meridian Labs. The Aster Program studies the Nereid Basin using the Atlas Sensor. Meridian Labs supplies the Atlas Sensor to Helios Research Institute. The program operates from Zephyr Station.

In 2022, Helios Research Institute approved the Aster Program. In 2024, the Aster Program expanded its Nereid Basin observations.

The 2024 licensing record states that Meridian Labs licensed the Atlas Sensor design to Helios Research Institute for the Aster Program. The license covered three field units and calibration support. Nova Dynamics was not listed as a licensee in this record.

citations.snippet:
Helios Research Institute leads the Aster Program with Meridian Labs. The Aster Program studies the Nereid Basin using the Atlas Sensor. Meridian Labs supplies the Atlas Sensor to Helios Research Institute. The program operates from Zephyr Station.

In 2022, Helios Research Institute approved the Aster Program. In 2024, the Aster Program expanded its Nereid Basin observations.

The 2024 licensing record states that Meridian Labs licensed the Atlas Sensor design to Helios Research Institute for the Aster Program. The license covered three field units and calibration support. Nova Dynamics was not listed as a licensee in this record.

Meridian Labs developed the Atlas Sensor for the Aster Program. The Atlas Sensor sends measurements to Zephyr Station. Zephyr Station forwards processed observations to Helios Research Institute. Meridian Labs maintains the sensor calibration archive.

In March 2024, Meridian Labs delivered the third Atlas Sensor to Zephyr Station. The delivery replaced the prototype sensor used in 2023.

Celeste Analytics analyzed the observations from Zephyr Station and the Atlas Sensor. Celeste Analytics concluded that the Lumen Shelf is the most methane-rich area in the Nereid Basin. Helios Research Institute used the conclusion to prioritize another Aster Program survey.

The causal chain recorded in the report is: Atlas Sensor measurements enabled Zephyr Station processing; Zephyr Station pro

Zephyr Station monitors the Nereid Basin. The Nereid Basin contains the Lumen Shelf, where methane readings are highest. Atlas Sensor observations from Zephyr Station helped Helios Research Institute map the Lumen Shelf.

After the 2024 expansion, Zephyr Station recorded methane and water-vapor signatures at the Lumen Shelf. The findings were reviewed by Meridian Labs.

Zephyr Station monitors the Nereid Basin. The Nereid Basin contains the Lumen Shelf, where methane readings are highest. Atlas Sensor observations from Zephyr Station helped Helios Research Institute map the Lumen Shelf.

After the 2024 expansion, Zephyr Station recorded methane and water-vapor signatures at the Lumen Shelf. The findings were reviewed by Meridian Labs.

Celeste Analytics analyzed the observations from Zephyr Station and the Atlas Sensor. Celeste Analytics concluded that the Lumen Shelf is the most methane-rich area in the Nereid Basin. Helios Research Institute used the conclusion to prioritize another Aster Program survey.

The causal chain recorded in the report is: Atlas Sensor measurements enabled Zephyr Station processing; Zephyr Station processing enabled the Lumen Shelf map; the map caused the next survey to prioritize the Lumen Shelf.
